Thank you for sharing something so personal—this cycle sounds exhausting, and the fact that you're seeking ways to break it shows real self-awareness and strength.

A few things that many people find helpful: try to notice early signs of stress and build in non-food coping tools ahead of time, like a walk, calling someone, journaling, or a brief breathing practice. When a binge urge hits, "urge surfing"—pausing and letting the wave pass without acting for even a few minutes—can create space. Eating regular, balanced meals also reduces the physical drive to binge, and practicing self-compassion instead of shame tends to break the binge-then-punish loop more effectively than harsh rules.

That said, patterns involving bingeing followed by compensatory exercise can be signs of an eating disorder, and you deserve real support. I'd gently encourage reaching out to a doctor or therapist who specializes in eating concerns. In the US, the NEDA Helpline (1-800-931-2237) can point you toward resources. You don't have to manage this alone.
